cells.tense: You are here with the strength to hold and to keep going while the work takes shape.
cells.ask: Walk around what you have built and say out loud what it can now carry on its own. Then leave your hands still and let one next step wait.
cells.core:
You are the one holding this, and it shows. You have put in the long steady effort through the hard parts, not just the bright ones. What is in front of you stands because you kept at it.

The part that is working matches the load: you carry without forcing the outcome, letting what you have made take its own shape. No one had to hand you the pen. You can bear what is heavy and still keep the room gentle. That is the strength here, the plain inner kind that does not need an audience. Keep feeding it by letting the work breathe on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You hold it steady and it stands because you did the hard parts.
cells.verb: Finishing what has been built and letting it stand.
cells.place: In the room where something is being grown and tended.

cells.tense: You are reaching ahead to a version of the finished thing that does not exist yet.
cells.ask: Set down the plan for one day. Look at only what is already in front of you, and let that be enough until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You can already see the finished shape. That is why you are running the steps in your head before the ground is ready. The reach keeps you focused on a future that cannot be written in yet, so the stretch does not rest. Some of your strength goes to problems that have not arrived.

Your care is still real, but it strains against what is still opening. Try this instead: set the plan down for one day. Look at what is already in front of you and let it be enough until tomorrow. The build can wait for its real timing. Let one thing arrive without being managed into place first.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have already built that no one can take back. Say it out loud once, and let it count.
cells.core:
Somewhere you learned that this kind of care means waiting until it is safe to say you are finished, so you stopped saying it at all. You still tend what is growing, but you stand back from calling any of your own work done. The door is behind you and you are still guarding it.

What is missing in the room is the clear eye that lets a thing count. Try it: name one thing you have already built that no one can take back. Say it out loud once, and let it count. Nothing has to be proven, only seen. One true line about your own work, spoken plainly, gives the weight back to what you have carried.
cells.sheetLine: You keep tending and you will not call any of it done.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what grows here while treating it as something that happened on its own.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have kept alive and say plainly, that was your doing. No credit ceremony, just the plain sentence.
cells.core:
You are the one in the room where things are growing. Your steady hands decide what gets tended, what gets left, and what quietly thrives. You describe it as if the conditions were simply there. The care is doing its work; the saying-so is not.

The pen is already in your hand and you have been writing it off as circumstance. Try one plain sentence: that was your doing. Choose one thing you kept alive and say it without ceremony. Nothing needs proving here. Seeing your own hand in the work is the start of clear sight, and clear sight is what has been missing.
cells.sheetLine: You have already made this grow. You just have not said so.
